chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi informed me from al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab al-Jumahi, who narrated from Muslim ibn Abdillah al-Basri, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Nahdi, from Shu'ba, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Habba ibn al-Urani, who said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, saying:

'I fear for you about two things: long ambitions and following base desires. As for long ambitions, they cause one to forget the Hereafter. And as for following desires, they divert from the Truth. Indeed, this world has departed turning its back, and the Hereafter has arrived facing you. Each of them has its sons, so be the sons of the Hereafter and do not be the sons of this world. For today there are deeds and no reckoning, and tomorrow there is reckoning and no deeds.'

key_terms.أبناء الآخرة: sons of the Hereafter - those who prioritize the next life
key_terms.اتباع الهوى: following desires - submission to base passions
key_terms.طول الأمل: long ambitions - excessive worldly hopes that breed heedlessness

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the dangers of long ambitions and following desires?
ai.summary: This sermon of Imam Ali, delivered to his followers in Kufa, warns against two spiritual diseases: long-term worldly ambitions that make one forget death and the afterlife, and following one's base desires which obstruct the path to truth. The metaphor of the world 'departing' and the hereafter 'arriving' conveys urgency, and the powerful closing aphorism -- 'today is for deeds without reckoning, tomorrow is for reckoning without deeds' -- is among Imam Ali's most quoted sayings.
